instrument_name: La. R.S. 23:632 Liability of employer for failure to pay; attorney fees; good-faith exception
figure_or_rule_carried: Section 632 is the penalty-wage remedy for failing to comply with R.S. 23:631: the lesser of 90 days wages at the daily rate or full wages from demand until payment (A); a good-faith dispute limits liability to the wages in dispute plus judicial interest (B); attorney fees (C). Amended Acts 1964 No. 422, 1977 No. 317, 2014 No. 750. It imposes no itemized pay-statement duty.

instrument_name: Massachusetts Constitution, Amendments Art. LXXXIX (Home Rule; Art. II as restated) Section 7 Limitations on Local Powers
figure_or_rule_carried: Nothing in this article shall be deemed to grant to any city or town the power to (2) levy, assess and collect taxes, provided the foregoing enumerated powers may be granted by the general court. A Massachusetts city or town therefore has no home-rule power to tax wages; any local tax needs a grant from the General Court (the local options are listed in US-MAR3-002 and US-MAR3-003).

instrument_name: Mass.gov DOR Tax Rates (updated 2025-12-30): list of Massachusetts taxes and local options
figure_or_rule_carried: ABSENCE (Medium-High): the page lists every tax by type and rate (income incl. wage withholding 5.00% with 4% surtax above 1,107,750 for tax year 2026; estate; alcohol; tobacco; deeds; motor fuels; room occupancy; sales/use; meals; marijuana; corporate; insurance; ship; Boston surcharges) and names the only local options: local room occupancy up to 6% (6.5% Boston), community impact fee up to 3%, local meals tax 0.75%, marijuana up to 3%, jet fuel at local option. instrument_name: Mass.gov DLS Local Option Excise Taxes
authority: Massachusetts DOR Division of Local Services
figure_or_rule_carried: Cities and towns may adopt excise statutes on meals (0.75%), rooms (up to 6%; 6.5% Boston; short-term rental community impact fee up to 3%) and recreational marijuana (up to 3%). This DLS page covers locally adopted excises only (it does not list property tax); it corroborates US-MAR3-002.

instrument_name: Michigan Treasury FAQ: Which cities impose an income tax? (re-read)
figure_or_rule_carried: Exist: yes, 24 cities levy municipal taxes related to income (individual, business incl. withholding, fiduciary). Collector: Treasury administers City of Detroit income taxes; 23 cities administer their own forms, filing, payment and taxpayer support: Albion, Battle Creek, Benton Harbor, Big Rapids, East Lansing, Grand Rapids, Flint, Grayling, Hamtramck, Highland Park, Hudson, Ionia, Jackson, Lansing, Lapeer, Muskegon, Muskegon Heights, Pontiac, Port Huron, Portland, Saginaw, Springfield, Walker. Same content as US-MI-P5-2-002 and US-MI-LOC-001.

instrument_name: Michigan Treasury City Tax Administration 5469 (Rev. 05-25) 2026 City of Detroit Income Tax Withholding Guide
authority: Michigan Department of Treasury - City Tax Administration
article_or_section: pp.1-2 Who Must Withhold; Income Tax Rates; Calculating the Amount to Withhold
figure_or_rule_carried: Detroit 2026: employers with a location or doing business in Detroit withhold for Detroit residents (wherever they work) and for nonresidents whose predominant place of employment is Detroit; rates 2.4% residents, 1.2% nonresidents; exemption 600.00 per year (weekly 11.54, biweekly 23.08, semi-monthly 25.00, monthly 50.00, daily 1.64); employee certificate DW-4 Form 5527 kept by the employer; returns Monthly Form 5323 and Annual Reconciliation Form 5321; no Form 5527 means withhold at the resident rate with no exemptions. Treasury administers Detroit.

instrument_name: City Income Tax Act, Act 284 of 1964, Chapter 2 Uniform City Income Tax Ordinance, MCL 141.611 (Sec. 11)
figure_or_rule_carried: Uniform ordinance rate: annual tax of 1% on corporations and resident individuals and 1/2% on nonresident individuals; a lower rate if the city governing body so resolves, and the nonresident rate may not exceed 1/2 of the resident rate. Last amended by Act 233 of 1995 (effective 1995-12-19). Cities above the uniform rate rely on the MCL 141.503 and 141.503a ceilings (US-MI-P5-2-003). City rates other than Detroit (US-MIR3-002) are set by each city ordinance and were NOT read from city sources.
